title: Defining Items

children:
If you do not want to interface item records from the ERP, 
 you can define them in SCALE. By defining an item in the system, you can 
 manage how its processed, what allocation and locating rules are applied 
 to it, and what handling controls (lot controlled, etc) are required during 
 processing. Item setup is optional. If you do not want to create records 
 on the Item Window, the system will reference the item values defined 
 on the shipment line records.

You 
 will use these fields to identify the item, its format and the company 
 that distributes it.

Use the Item Template Field 
 to define how the item name is structured. As soon as you provide a value 
 here, the Item Field input fields will accommodate the item template's 
 structure. Note that this field is not required. 
 If you don't select an item template, the Item Field will be a free-format 
 field.

If appropriate, use the Company 
 Field to identify the company that will distribute this item. If 
 your warehouse supports multi-company processing, you need to associate 
 each item with the company that sells it. Therefore, if two or more companies 
 use the same value to identify in item, the system can discern which record 
 associated with each company.

Use the Item 
 Field and Description fields to identify the product. Provide a 
 name for this record in the Item Field; this field is alpha-numeric. Provide 
 a description. Generally, the values defined in both the Item Field and 
 the Description Field are displayed together. Therefore, if the value 
 in the Item Field is numeric, the user can reference the description value 
 to visually identify the item during processing.

You will use these fields to identify the item, its format 
 and the company that distributes it.

Use the Allocation Rule Field 
 to associate this item with an allocation rule. An allocation rule determines 
 how the system will select allocation locations. If an item has unique 
 requirements, associate it with an allocation rule that meets its needs. 
 The system will reference this field if an allocation rule was not define 
 on the shipment line.

Use the Locating Rule Field 
 to associate this item with a locating rule. A locating rule determines 
 how the system will locate this product to storage locations. The system 
 will reference this field if a locating rule was not defined on the receipt 
 container record. Note that this rule can be overridden if the Always Override setting was selected on the locating rule assignment record.

Select the Inventory Tracking Checkbox 
 to track which locations this item is stored in and how many units are 
 associated with each location. The system will use this information to 
 perform allocations and replenishments. This value will already be selected 
 if the Track Inventory Option is selected on the Inventory System Value 
 Window.

If appropriate, 
 use the NMFC 
 Code Field to associate an NMFC 
 to this item. The NMFC 
 code links an item to a class for freight rating purposes. Each NMFC 
 value is a sequence of letters and/or numbers representing a group of 
 like items with similar characteristics. It is used primarily by LTL 
 carriers.

If appropriate, use the Item Class 
 Field to associate a class to this item. An item class identifies 
 a group of items that share common characteristics, such as unit of measure 
 values and container dimensions. You can use item classes to manage the 
 movement of like items through the warehouse. This is especially helpful 
 for items that share the physical dimensions and space requirements. For 
 example, if your warehouse distributes movie DVDs, 
 you could associate all individual DVDs 
 with the DVD item class.

Use the Packing Class Field 
 to link this item to a packing class. A packing class identifies items 
 that can be shipped in the same container. Packing classes also identify 
 which containers this item can be packed into.

Use the Storage 
 Template Field to associate this item with a storage template. 
 A storage template groups together quantity UM 
 values that service a general type of product, like liquid, gas, or solid 
 products.

WARNING: If you change the storage template on an item to one 
 that has a different base unit of measure, the system will change the 
 UM on all related data, such as existing inventory, open shipments, and 
 open receipts.

Using the Item Characteristics 
 (1) Tab Fields

You will use these fields to define the basic 
 characteristics for your item.

Use the Division 
 and Department Fields to associate these values to the item.

Use the Item 
 Size Field to indicate the size of the item, such as S, M, L, XL.

Use the Item 
 Color Field to indicate the color of the item.

Use the Item 
 Style Field to indicate the style of the item.

Use the Shipment BOM 
 Action Field:See 
 the

Using the Item Characteristics 
 (2) Tab Fields

You will use these fields to further define the 
 basic characteristics for your item.

Use the Cost 
 Field to indicate the net cost of this item.

Use the List 
 Price Field to indicate the original price for this item.

Use the Net Price 
 Field to indicate the discounted price for this item.

Use the EPC Company 
 Prefix Field to indicate the pre-defined identifier for a company 
 associated with a particular item. This value is used when the system 
 computes an Electronic Product Code (EPC).

Use the EPC Item 
 Reference Field to indicate the identifier that is given to this 
 item and its packing level (unit, inner-pack, case, or pallet). This value 
 is used when the system computes an Electronic Product Code (EPC).

Use the CAGE 
 Code Field to identify that this item is associated with a company 
 that does business with the United States Federal Government. The format 
 of this is a five-position code, where the first and fifth position must 
 be a numeric character. The second, third and fourth positions may be 
 any mixture of alpha/numeric characters (excluding "I" and "O"). 
 All positions are non-significant. Note that if you need to obtain a CAGE 
 Code, contact the Defense Logistics Information Service (DLIS).

GTIN Enabled 
 Checkbox: See the topic

Enabling GTIN On 
 Item Or Item Cross Reference

The FedEx ITN 
 (Internal Transaction Number) Field  is 
 given by AES after an SED is submitted to them, and it is unique per shipment.

The FedEx XTN 
 (External Transaction Number) Field is an exemption number for 
 this item provided by the government.

You can use 
 these check boxes 
 to identify how the product will be processed through the system.

Use the Immediate 
 Needs Fields to make this item
for immediate needs processing; and the
that the system will use when processing this item.

Use the Inbound 
 QC Fields to make this item
for inbound quality control processing; and the

that the system 
 will use when processing this item. Also, you can use the

field to further define the quantity you want the system to send 
 to QC.

You can use these check boxes 
 to identify how the product will be processed through the system.

Select the Catch Weight 
 Required Checkbox to require employees 
 to identify this item's weight during packing/unpacking. Note that an 
 item cannot be validated for both catch weight and a serial number.

Select the Lot 
 Controlled Checkbox to require employees to identify this item's 
 lot during packing/unpacking.

Use the Lot Template 
 Field to associate this item with a lot template. These templates 
 define a lot ID's structure.

Use the Days To Expire Field 
 to indicate the number of days that the system will add (to today's date) 
 in order to calculate a lot's expiration date. Note that this value will 
 not be honored if the lot already has an existing expiration date.

NOTE: If you enter a 0 
 into this field, the system will not add any additional days when assigning 
 an expiration date.

Use the Serial Number option checkboxes to determine how the system will track 
 serial numbers for this item. You will need to first choose which warehouse 
 flow (Inbound, Inventory, or Outbound) for which you want the system to 
 track serial numbers.

The application allows you to track serial numbers in the following 
 combinations:

Use the Template 
 Field to select a serial number template that the system will use 
 for computation. You can also choose to not select a template, and then 
 the user will be able to enter any combination of characters for a serial 
 number.

Using the Internet 
 Information Tab Fields

You can use these fields to define web-specific 
 item settings.

You can use these fields to have the system suggest an appropriate replacement item to be used on a shipment line instead of the original item. Alternate/substitute items are available only when entering order/shipment lines on the Shipment Line Screen and the Order Entry Window. This functionality is not available when entering order/shipment lines using TPM Order Entry or the Order Download interface. Also note that you must activate 
 the "Availability Checking" value on the Inventory Control Values 
 Window if you want the system to check to see if an ordered item is currently 
 in stock in the warehouse.

Use the Alternate Item Field 
 to associate an alternate item with the current item. Typically, you would use an alternate 
 item when you have designated the current item as obsolete or 
 permanently out of stock. When an alternate item designation exists for an item, the system will alert the user 
 that they are about to order an obsolete item, and that an alternate item 
 is available. The user can then decide whether or not to use this alternate item
 on their order/shipment line.

Use the Substitute 
 Item Field to associate substitute item(s) 
 with the current item. You can use substitute item(s) to replace the original 
 item if there is not enough quantity available in the warehouse. When entering an order/shipment line,  the system will alert you that the desired item is not in 
 stock, and that a substitute item exists. The user can then decide whether or not to 
 use the substitute item on their order/shipment line.

- You can enter more than one substitute item (the system will add it to the list box under the Substitute Item Field); the system will process through these items in sequential order, and choose the first one that can completely fulfill the original item's requested quantity.
- The item(s) you choose as substitutes must have the same company designation as the original item.

- Only one level of substitution is supported. For example, suppose Item A has Item B defined as its substitute, and Item B in turn has Item C defined as its substitute. The system will not suggest Item C when there is not enough inventory for Item A or Item B. The system will suggest Item B if Item A is lacking, but there is enough quantity of Item B to meet the request. The system will make no suggestion when neither Item A nor Item B can meet the request; Item A will be applied to the line, and allocation of Item A may fail during the wave if inventory is not available at that time.

- The system will suggest a substitute only if the substitute item defined can fulfill the entire shipment line quantity. For example, suppose Item A has Item B defined as its substitute, and the available inventory is 5 EA for Item A and 5 EA for Item B. If the shipment line has a request  for 10 EA of Item A, the system will not substitute the remaining 5 EA with Item B.

You will use these fields if Progistics 
 generates international documentation for the item. If you do not ship 
 to international markets, do not provide values on this tab.

The Preference Criterion Field identifies where all raw materials container in the item originated from. This information can be obtained from the United States government: This value is printed on the NAFTA Certificate of Origin. Please see the

Use the Harmonized Code Field 
 to define this product's harmonize code. This is a universal value, assigned 
 by the government, that identifies product on an international shipment. 
 This is a required field.

Use the Net Cost Buttons to 
 determine if an item is subject to a regional value content requirement. Please see the

Use the Country of Origin Field 
 to identify the country where this item was manufactured. This is a required 
 field.

Select the Producer 
 Checkbox if the entity shipping an item is the same one who manufactured 
 it. Please see the

You will use these fields if you want to associate 
 a category to an item record. You can use these categories to hold user-defined 
 information.

Use the Category 
 Fields to choose an item category to associate with this item. 
 See the field topic

If appropriate, use the Company 
 Field to identify the company that will distribute this item. If 
 your warehouse supports multi-company processing, you need to associate 
 each item with the company that sells it. Therefore, if two or more companies 
 use the same value to identify in item, the system can discern which record 
 associated with each company.

                
 

            

            
Use the Item 
 Field and Description fields to identify the product. Provide a 
 name for this record in the Item Field; this field is alpha-numeric. Provide 
 a description. Generally, the values defined in both the Item Field and 
 the Description Field are displayed together. Therefore, if the value 
 in the Item Field is numeric, the user can reference the description value 
 to visually identify the item during processing.

        

        
 

        
Using the General Tab 
 Fields

        
You will use these fields to identify the item, its format 
 and the company that distributes it.

        

            

                
Use the Allocation Rule Field 
 to associate this item with an allocation rule. An allocation rule determines 
 how the system will select allocation locations. If an item has unique 
 requirements, associate it with an allocation rule that meets its needs. 
 The system will reference this field if an allocation rule was not define 
 on the shipment line.

                
 

            

            

                
Use the Locating Rule Field 
 to associate this item with a locating rule. A locating rule determines 
 how the system will locate this product to storage locations. The system 
 will reference this field if a locating rule was not defined on the receipt 
 container record. Note that this rule can be overridden if the Always Override setting was selected on the locating rule assignment record.

                
 

            

            

                
Select the Inventory Tracking Checkbox 
 to track which locations this item is stored in and how many units are 
 associated with each location. The system will use this information to 
 perform allocations and replenishments. This value will already be selected 
 if the Track Inventory Option is selected on the Inventory System Value 
 Window.

                
 

            

            
If appropriate, 
 use the NMFC 
 Code Field to associate an NMFC 
 to this item. The NMFC 
 code links an item to a class for freight rating purposes. Each NMFC 
 value is a sequence of letters and/or numbers representing a group of 
 like items with similar characteristics. It is used primarily by LTL 
 carriers.

 

            

                
If appropriate, use the Item Class 
 Field to associate a class to this item. An item class identifies 
 a group of items that share common characteristics, such as unit of measure 
 values and container dimensions. You can use item classes to manage the 
 movement of like items through the warehouse. This is especially helpful 
 for items that share the physical dimensions and space requirements. For 
 example, if your warehouse distributes movie DVDs, 
 you could associate all individual DVDs 
 with the DVD item class.

                
 

            

            

                
Use the Packing Class Field 
 to link this item to a packing class. A packing class identifies items 
 that can be shipped in the same container. Packing classes also identify 
 which containers this item can be packed into.

                
 

            

            
Use the Storage 
 Template Field to associate this item with a storage template. 
 A storage template groups together quantity UM 
 values that service a general type of product, like liquid, gas, or solid 
 products. 



WARNING: If you change the storage template on an item to one 
 that has a different base unit of measure, the system will change the 
 UM on all related data, such as existing inventory, open shipments, and 
 open receipts.

        

        
 

        
Using the Item Characteristics 
 (1) Tab Fields

        
You will use these fields to define the basic 
 characteristics for your item.

        

            
Use the Division 
 and Department Fields to associate these values to the item.

 

            
Use the Item 
 Size Field to indicate the size of the item, such as S, M, L, XL. 
 

 

            
Use the Item 
 Color Field to indicate the color of the item.

 

            
Use the Item 
 Style Field to indicate the style of the item.

 

            
Use the Shipment BOM 
 Action Field:See 
 the field topic for a description.

        

        
 

        
Using the Item Characteristics 
 (2) Tab Fields

        
You will use these fields to further define the 
 basic characteristics for your item.

        

            
Use the Cost 
 Field to indicate the net cost of this item.

 

            
Use the List 
 Price Field to indicate the original price for this item.

 

            
Use the Net Price 
 Field to indicate the discounted price for this item.

 

            
Use the EPC Company 
 Prefix Field to indicate the pre-defined identifier for a company 
 associated with a particular item. This value is used when the system 
 computes an Electronic Product Code (EPC).

 

            
Use the EPC Item 
 Reference Field to indicate the identifier that is given to this 
 item and its packing level (unit, inner-pack, case, or pallet). This value 
 is used when the system computes an Electronic Product Code (EPC).

 

            
Use the CAGE 
 Code Field to identify that this item is associated with a company 
 that does business with the United States Federal Government. The format 
 of this is a five-position code, where the first and fifth position must 
 be a numeric character. The second, third and fourth positions may be 
 any mixture of alpha/numeric characters (excluding "I" and "O"). 
 All positions are non-significant. Note that if you need to obtain a CAGE 
 Code, contact the Defense Logistics Information Service (DLIS).

 

            
GTIN Enabled 
 Checkbox: See the topic            Enabling GTIN On 
 Item Or Item Cross Reference for information on this field. 

 

            
The FedEx ITN 
 (Internal Transaction Number) Field  is 
 given by AES after an SED is submitted to them, and it is unique per shipment.

 

            
The FedEx XTN 
 (External Transaction Number) Field is an exemption number for 
 this item provided by the government.

        

        
 

        
Using the Handling 
 (1) Tab Fields

        
You can use 
 these check boxes 
 to identify how the product will be processed through the system.

        

            
Use the Immediate 
 Needs Fields to make this item            eligible 
 for immediate needs processing; and the            locating 
 rule that the system will use when processing this item.

 

            
Use the Inbound 
 QC Fields to make this item            eligible 
 for inbound quality control processing; and the            locating 
 rule and            UM that the system 
 will use when processing this item. Also, you can use the            Compute 
 Quantity As buttons and the            Inspection 
 Qty field to further define the quantity you want the system to send 
 to QC.

        

        
 

        
Using the Handling 
 (2) Tab Fields

        
You can use these check boxes 
 to identify how the product will be processed through the system.

        

            
Select the Catch Weight 
 Required Checkbox to require employees 
 to identify this item's weight during packing/unpacking. Note that an 
 item cannot be validated for both catch weight and a serial number.

 

            
Select the Lot 
 Controlled Checkbox to require employees to identify this item's 
 lot during packing/unpacking.

 

            
Use the Lot Template 
 Field to associate this item with a lot template. These templates 
 define a lot ID's structure. 

 

            

                
Use the Days To Expire Field 
 to indicate the number of days that the system will add (to today's date) 
 in order to calculate a lot's expiration date. Note that this value will 
 not be honored if the lot already has an existing expiration date.

 

                
NOTE: If you enter a 0 
 into this field, the system will not add any additional days when assigning 
 an expiration date.

                
 

            

            
Use the Serial Number option checkboxes to determine how the system will track 
 serial numbers for this item. You will need to first choose which warehouse 
 flow (Inbound, Inventory, or Outbound) for which you want the system to 
 track serial numbers. 



The application allows you to track serial numbers in the following 
 combinations:



- Inbound only

- Inventory only

- Outbound only

- Inbound and 
 Outbound

- Inbound and 
 Inventory            and 
 Outbound

 

            
Use the Template 
 Field to select a serial number template that the system will use 
 for computation. You can also choose to not select a template, and then 
 the user will be able to enter any combination of characters for a serial 
 number.

        

        
 

        
Using the Internet 
 Information Tab Fields

        
You can use these fields to define web-specific 
 item settings.

        
 

        
Using the Alternate/Substitute 
 Tab Fields

        
You can use these fields to have the system suggest an appropriate replacement item to be used on a shipment line instead of the original item. Alternate/substitute items are available only when entering order/shipment lines on the Shipment Line Screen and the Order Entry Window. This functionality is not available when entering order/shipment lines using TPM Order Entry or the Order Download interface. Also note that you must activate 
 the "Availability Checking" value on the Inventory Control Values 
 Window if you want the system to check to see if an ordered item is currently 
 in stock in the warehouse.

        

            

                
Use the Alternate Item Field 
 to associate an alternate item with the current item. Typically, you would use an alternate 
 item when you have designated the current item as obsolete or 
 permanently out of stock. When an alternate item designation exists for an item, the system will alert the user 
 that they are about to order an obsolete item, and that an alternate item 
 is available. The user can then decide whether or not to use this alternate item
 on their order/shipment line.

                
 

            

            
Use the Substitute 
 Item Field to associate substitute item(s) 
 with the current item. You can use substitute item(s) to replace the original 
 item if there is not enough quantity available in the warehouse. When entering an order/shipment line,  the system will alert you that the desired item is not in 
 stock, and that a substitute item exists. The user can then decide whether or not to 
 use the substitute item on their order/shipment line.     



- You can enter more than one substitute item (the system will add it to the list box under the Substitute Item Field); the system will process through these items in sequential order, and choose the first one that can completely fulfill the original item's requested quantity. 



- The item(s) you choose as substitutes must have the same company designation as the original item.



- Only one level of substitution is supported. For example, suppose Item A has Item B defined as its substitute, and Item B in turn has Item C defined as its substitute. The system will not suggest Item C when there is not enough inventory for Item A or Item B. The system will suggest Item B if Item A is lacking, but there is enough quantity of Item B to meet the request. The system will make no suggestion when neither Item A nor Item B can meet the request; Item A will be applied to the line, and allocation of Item A may fail during the wave if inventory is not available at that time.



- The system will suggest a substitute only if the substitute item defined can fulfill the entire shipment line quantity. For example, suppose Item A has Item B defined as its substitute, and the available inventory is 5 EA for Item A and 5 EA for Item B. If the shipment line has a request  for 10 EA of Item A, the system will not substitute the remaining 5 EA with Item B.

        

        
 

        
Using the International 
 Tab Fields

        
You will use these fields if Progistics 
 generates international documentation for the item. If you do not ship 
 to international markets, do not provide values on this tab.

        

            

                
The Preference Criterion Field identifies where all raw materials container in the item originated from. This information can be obtained from the United States government: This value is printed on the NAFTA Certificate of Origin. Please see the field topic for more information. 
 

                
 

            

            

                
Use the Harmonized Code Field 
 to define this product's harmonize code. This is a universal value, assigned 
 by the government, that identifies product on an international shipment. 
 This is a required field.

                
 

            

            

                
Use the Net Cost Buttons to 
 determine if an item is subject to a regional value content requirement. Please see the         field topic for more information.

                
 

            

            

                
Use the Country of Origin Field 
 to identify the country where this item was manufactured. This is a required 
 field.

                
 

            

            
Select the Producer 
 Checkbox if the entity shipping an item is the same one who manufactured 
 it. Please see the field topic for more information.

        

        
 

        
Using the Categories 
 Tab Fields

        
You will use these fields if you want to associate 
 a category to an item record. You can use these categories to hold user-defined 
 information.

        

            
Use the Category 
 Fields to choose an item category to associate with this item. 
 See the field topic            Item Categories 
 1-10 for more information.
